dismissals.because: src/forge/templates/conventions/frontend.md:61 Done-when 3 asks that production never shows the toolbar; the run-time check never loads its chunk outside APP_ENV=demo, and one Dockerfile builds one image for both, so a separate production build adds a moving part the item doesn't need

findings.body: The example uses `__APP_ENV__` both as the window property name and as the value to replace. Following the backend instruction to replace `__APP_ENV__` in `index.html` changes the property name first; replacing every occurrence changes it too. The app then reads an unset `window.__APP_ENV__`, so the toolbar never appears in the demo. Use a replacement token that does not occur in the property name.
findings.title: Not done: Anyone can point at the screen

findings.body: The functional check claims the demo-data refusal gives a plain next step. For the likely case of tables that already contain rows, the sample only logs that fact. It does not tell the operator to use an empty demo database or what to do before retrying, so the claimed next-step check is unsupported.
findings.title: Not done: functional check

findings.body: The sample counts tables before opening the insertion transaction. A previous instance can write a real row after the counts and before the demo transaction, especially during the overlapping deployment described in `src/forge/templates/conventions/deploy.md:5-6`. The loader would then mix demo and real rows despite its refusal rule. Guard the check and insertion against a concurrent first write.
findings.title: Make the empty-table check atomic with demo insertion

findings.body: The stack convention tells builders to add a first-version loader, but the skill's prototype instructions at `src/forge/templates/skill.md:118-127` still do not tell the agent to build it or use the Words they use list for screen labels. The story assigns skill edits to SPEC, outside this task's scope.
